turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Well, thank you for seeing me. I'm here because... well, it's about bridges. 

The moment I realize that crossing a bridge is unavoidable, my heart just starts pounding. My hands get all damp on the steering wheel, or on the armrest if I'm riding with someone else. It's just this terrible rush of fear that hits me before I'm even on the bridge.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient identifies a marked fear centered on bridges, which fits a situational specific phobia.
symptom_reasoning.S063: The patient describes an immediate rush of fear and autonomic arousal (pounding heart, damp hands) the moment crossing a bridge is unavoidable.

turns.doctor_question: Do you experience this kind of fear in situations other than crossing bridges?
turns.patient_response: No, no, it's really just the bridges. I mean, I know perfectly well that thousands of cars cross those bridges every single day. But... well, when I see a high span coming up on the map, or if I spot it ahead through the windshield, logic just goes out the window. It feels to me as if the whole thing is just waiting to drop away right from under us.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient confirms an intense fear specific to bridges, noting that despite knowing thousands of cars cross safely, they feel the bridge is waiting to collapse under them.

turns.doctor_question: Is your fear of crossing bridges related to how high the bridge is?
turns.patient_response: I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't really noticed if it's specifically about the height. It just seems to be... well, the act of crossing them at all that sets me off.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient confirms that the act of crossing bridges triggers their fear, reflecting a situational specific phobic fear.

turns.doctor_question: Does your fear occur when you're walking across a bridge, or is it primarily when you're driving or riding in a vehicle?
turns.patient_response: Well, I'm not entirely sure about walking. I haven't actually tried to walk across a bridge in... well, in years, to be honest. So I can't really say for sure how I'd feel doing that. I just know it happens when I'm in a vehicle, whether I'm the one driving or just riding along in the passenger seat. That's primarily what I have to deal with.

turns.doctor_question: Would your fear occur if you were crossing the bridge by train?
turns.patient_response: I really couldn't say. I haven't been on a train in... well, it's been decades, to be honest. So I just don't know if that same panic would happen or not, since I haven't had the chance to find out.

turns.doctor_question: Do you think your fear would occur if you were crossing a bridge on a bus?
turns.patient_response: I'm not sure about a bus, either. I don't really take the bus these days, so I haven't been in that situation. I imagine it might be similar to being in a car, but I just don't know for a fact since I haven't tried it.

turns.doctor_question: Do you think your fear would be less intense if you were driving or riding in a vehicle on a bridge that you had crossed many times before?
turns.patient_response: No, I don't think it would make a difference. Even if it's a bridge I've been over a hundred times, the feeling is exactly the same. The panic just hits me, no matter how familiar it is.

symptom_reasoning.S063: The patient states that crossing a bridge invariably triggers panic regardless of how familiar it is, indicating an immediate fear and anxiety response to the phobic stimulus.

turns.doctor_question: Would your fear of crossing the bridge occur if you were walking across it alone?
turns.patient_response: I really don't know. I haven't... well, I haven't tried walking across a bridge in a very long time. At my age, I don't really walk those kinds of distances anyway. So I just don't have a good answer for you on that one, since I haven't been in that situation to find out.

turns.doctor_question: Do you think your fear of bridges would occur if you were in a vehicle that was stopped on the bridge, not moving?
turns.patient_response: I couldn't tell you for sure. I avoid bridges so much these days that I haven't been stuck in traffic on one in years. I imagine just being up there, even parked, would still be awful, but... well, I just don't have a definite answer for you since I haven't been in that exact situation to find out.

symptom_reasoning.S064: The patient explicitly confirms active avoidance of the phobic situation by stating that they avoid bridges so much that they haven't been on one in years.

turns.doctor_question: Would your fear of crossing the bridge occur if you were in a vehicle that was driving onto a bridge that was closed to pedestrians, but open to vehicles?
turns.patient_response: I honestly don't know. Whether there are people walking on it or not... I haven't really paid attention to that. I just avoid bridges altogether, so I couldn't say if that would make a difference.

symptom_reasoning.S064: The patient explicitly confirms avoiding the phobic situation by stating, 'I just avoid bridges altogether.'

turns.doctor_question: Do you think your fear of bridges would occur if you were a passenger on a motorcycle crossing the bridge?
turns.patient_response:
A motorcycle? Well... I haven't been on one of those in decades. I can't even imagine trying to cross a bridge on one at my age. 

I'm sure it would be absolutely terrifying, being right out in the open like that, but... I really have no idea. I just don't go near bridges at all, no matter what kind of vehicle it is.

symptom_reasoning.S064: The patient explicitly confirms active avoidance of bridges by stating that they do not go near bridges at all, regardless of the vehicle.

turns.doctor_question: Would your fear of crossing the bridge occur if you were in a different type of vehicle, such as a truck?
turns.patient_response: I really couldn't say. I don't ride in trucks these days, and like I mentioned, I just avoid bridges entirely. So I don't know if being in a bigger vehicle would make a difference or not. To me, a bridge is a bridge, and I just stay away from them no matter what I'm riding in.

symptom_reasoning.S064: The patient explicitly confirms active avoidance of the phobic situation, stating that they avoid bridges entirely and stay away from them regardless of the vehicle.

turns.doctor_question: Would your fear of crossing the bridge occur if you were in a vehicle that is completely enclosed, such as an RV?
turns.patient_response: I don't think it would matter if it was an RV or a car. An enclosed vehicle is still a vehicle on a bridge. Like I said, I just don't go on them at all anymore. I haven't tried crossing in an RV, but I'm certain I'd still be just as afraid.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient explicitly affirms that being on a bridge would still make them just as afraid, confirming situational specific phobic fear.
symptom_reasoning.S064: The patient confirms complete avoidance of bridges, stating 'I just don't go on them at all anymore.'

turns.doctor_question: Would your fear of crossing the bridge occur if you were in a boat going under the bridge?
turns.patient_response: Going under it? I don't know... I haven't been on a boat in years. But honestly, just the thought of being near one, even underneath, makes me uneasy. I couldn't tell you for sure because I just avoid them completely.

symptom_reasoning.S064: The patient explicitly confirms active avoidance of bridges, stating 'I just avoid them completely.'

turns.doctor_question: Would your fear of crossing the bridge occur if you were in a vehicle, but someone else was driving and you were not paying attention to the road or the bridge?
turns.patient_response: I really don't know for sure. I haven't been in a situation like that because, well, I just don't go near them at all anymore. I mean, even if someone else was at the wheel, I don't think I could just... turn my mind off and not pay attention. I'd know the bridge was coming. So I can't say for certain since I haven't tried it, but I imagine I'd still be just as terrified.

symptom_reasoning.S064: The patient explicitly reports active avoidance of the phobic situation by stating they do not go near bridges at all anymore.

turns.doctor_question: Would your fear occur if you were crossing the bridge as a pedestrian, but with someone else accompanying you?
turns.patient_response:
Walking? No, I... I wouldn't even attempt that. Having someone walking right next to me wouldn't really change anything. It's still a bridge, and I'd still be out there on it. 

I haven't done it, so I don't have a recent example to give you, but... I know I'd be just as frightened. I just stay away from them completely.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient describes marked fear of bridges regardless of accompaniment, confirming a specific situational fear.
symptom_reasoning.S064: The patient explicitly confirms active avoidance by stating they would not even attempt walking on a bridge and stay away from them completely.

turns.doctor_question: Would your fear of crossing the bridge occur if you were crossing it by a mode of transportation that is not a vehicle, such as a bicycle?
turns.patient_response:
A bicycle? Well, I haven't ridden a bike in a very long time... I'm 87, after all. But to answer your question, yes, I'm certain the fear would still be exactly the same. 

It really doesn't matter how I'm getting across. A car, walking, a bike... it's the bridge itself that causes the problem. I just wouldn't go near it.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient explicitly confirms having a marked fear of the bridge itself regardless of the mode of transportation (car, walking, or bicycle).
symptom_reasoning.S064: The patient demonstrates active phobic avoidance by stating, 'I just wouldn't go near it.'

turns.doctor_question: Would your fear of the bridge occur if you were in a vehicle that was crossing a bridge in a tunnel or an enclosed space?
turns.patient_response: I don't really know, to be honest. I haven't been in a situation like that... a bridge inside a tunnel. I'm not even sure if we have any of those around here. But given how I feel about bridges in general, I imagine I would still be very anxious. I just try to avoid them entirely, no matter what they look like.

symptom_reasoning.S064: The patient explicitly states that they try to avoid bridges entirely regardless of what they look like, confirming active phobic avoidance.

turns.doctor_question: Would your fear occur if you were on a bridge that was closed to traffic and you were just standing or sitting on it, not crossing it?
turns.patient_response: I don't think I could do that either. I mean, I haven't tried it, because I wouldn't even get close enough to find out. But just the thought of being on it, even if I wasn't moving... no, the fear would still be there. It's just being on the bridge at all that gets to me.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient describes persistent, marked fear provoked by the mere thought or presence on a bridge ('It's just being on the bridge at all that gets to me').
